A complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, purity, durability, reliability, safety or effectiveness, or performance of a drug or drug delivery system.
Adherence to all study-related, good clinical practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.
case report form; a printed, optical, or electronic document designed to record all of the protocol- required information to be reported to the sponsor for each study participant.

clinical research physician: Individual responsible for the medical conduct of the study. Responsibilities of the CRP may be performed by a physician, clinical research scientist, global safety physician or other medical officer.
The act of assigning a participant to a treatment. Participants who are enrolled in the study are those who have been assigned to a treatment.
Participants entered into a study are those who sign the ICF directly or through their legally acceptable representatives.

A process by which a participant voluntarily confirms their willingness to participate in a particular study, after having been informed of all aspects of the study that are relevant to the participant’s decision to participate. Informed consent is documented by means of a written, signed and dated ICF.

A pharmaceutical form of an active ingredient or placebo being tested or used as a reference in a clinical study, including products already on the market when used or assembled (formulated or packaged) in a way different from the authorized form, or marketed products used for an unauthorized indication, or marketed products used to gain further information about the authorized form.
Equivalent to CDISC term “subject”: an individual who participates in a clinical study, either as recipient of an investigational medicinal product or as a control
The act of determining if an individual meets minimum requirements to become part of a pool of potential candidates for participation in a clinical study.

Treatment-emergent adverse event: An untoward medical occurrence that emerges during a defined treatment period, having been absent pretreatment, or worsens relative to the pretreatment state, and does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.

notes: Single protocol version in the PDF: Protocol J2N-MC-JZNW Amendment (a), approved 22-Dec-2021 (pages 1-2); the SoA (pages 11-13) is from this version. The Amendment Summary of Changes (page 4) lists changes from the Original Protocol (22-Oct-2021), including 'Added footnote ‘g’ describing the allowed sampling windows for pirtobrutinib and rosuvastatin PK'; footnote g, together with SoA footnotes d and f and the last two SoA rows, is redacted ('CCI') on pages 12-13, so its content is not available. No SoA cross-references were given in the inputs; cross_references is empty. No questionnaires, rating scales, diaries or other instruments are named in the protocol; instruments is empty. Lab-tests table (Appendix 2, page 46) and the Appendix 6 liver follow-up table (pages 58-59) run their columns together in the text layer; both were read from the PDF page images (pages 46, 58, 59) before analytes were assigned to panels; quotes come from the text layer. Panels 1-8 are the Appendix 2 clinical laboratory tests, performed by the local laboratory (page 45). Panels 9-16 are the Appendix 6 liver-safety follow-up assessments (selected per Section 8.2.7.1, hepatic monitoring), analysed by the Lilly-designated central laboratory except Microbiology (investigator-designated local laboratory only) — a different lab from Appendix 2; both recorded. Panel names Hematology, Clinical Chemistry and Serology occur in both tables. Specimens for the panels are not stated except for the pregnancy test. Abbreviations: Appendix 7 list (pages 60-61, including glossary terms; 'investigation al product' is kept as split in the text layer), the SoA abbreviation line (page 13), the Appendix 2 table (page 46) and parenthetical definitions in the Appendix 6 table (pages 58-59, 'Hepatis B virus' as printed). Abbreviations defined only under other tables (e.g. FDA, INR on page 27) are not listed. SoA activity names: all tokens (CRU, PR, BP, ECG, PK) are defined; 'CCI' (two rows) is a redaction label, not an activity name, and no text describes those rows. Text describes procedures not visible as SoA rows: pirtobrutinib PK samples (Section 8.4 and the Blood Sampling Summary, page 47: 15 samples) and a separate blood sample for storage for potential pharmacogenetic analysis (Section 8.6; page 47: 'Pharmacogenetics for storage'); these may be the redacted 'CCI' rows. Appendix 5: Genetics (page 57) is redacted. The Rosuvastatin PK samples entry cites Section 8.4, which describes rosuvastatin and pirtobrutinib PK samples together. Updated 2026-11-07 to schema 1.1 (no re-extraction): instruments carry kind.
